142707378.title: GDPR ALERT: 4 data-subject request(s) pending past 25 days (GDPR Art.12(3) requires a response within 1 month). 4 already exceed the 30-day statutory deadline. These need manual action in the admin GDPR queue — there is no automated processor. Sample: #...
142707378.note: GDPR DSAR backlog alarm, and now a diagnosed defect in the alarm itself. Two separate things. (1) The backlog: same standing owner decision as NEXUS-PHP-4A (2026-08-13) - requests #6/#7/#8 (tenant 5) and #11 (tenant 11) are the owner's own admin test requests, so there is no Article 12(3) clock and nothing to action. (2) The respawn: commit 9ed9a316a (2026-08-13) tried to stop this alarm creating a fresh Sentry group every night by calling setFingerprint(['gdpr_request_overdue']) before Sentry\captureMessage(). That commit IS in the live release d0c34906ab49, and it has not worked - NEXUS-PHP-50 (24 Aug) and NEXUS-PHP-51 (25 Aug) are new groups on consecutive days. Root cause: OverdueGdprRequestCheck::raiseAlert() has TWO Sentry paths, and the fix only covered one. Leg 1 is Log::error($message, $context); production's LOG_STACK includes the 'sentry' log channel (config/logging.php:102), so that log line becomes its own Sentry event carrying NO fingerprint, grouped by message text. The message text embeds each request's age in days ('#6 t5 portability 71d'), which increments nightly, so every night is a new group. Proof from the NEXUS-PHP-51 event: tag logger=production and extra key 'log_context' - both signatures of the sentry-laravel LOG HANDLER, not of the explicit capture, whose context block would be named 'gdpr_requests'. Suggested fix (NOT applied - classified sensitive, needs owner authorisation): keep the ages out of the logged message string and pass them only in $context, or send leg 1 to a log channel that excludes sentry. Then one group whose event count is the age of the breach, as commit 9ed9a316a intended. Regression test should assert the logged message is byte-identical on two runs whose request ages differ.

143208420.title: Error: Call to a member function fetchColumn() on bool
143208420.note: GET /api/v2/admin/identity/audit-log returned 500 for every admin on every tenant, for the whole life of the endpoint. All three read methods in IdentityVerificationEventService called DB::statement(...)->fetchAll()/->fetchColumn(), but DB::statement() returns a bool, not a PDOStatement. Changed the reads to DB::select()/DB::selectOne() (the convention already used across app/Http/Controllers/Api/). The INSERT in log() was always correct and is unchanged, which is why events were recorded but never readable. New regression test tests/Laravel/Feature/Services/IdentityVerificationEventReadPathTest.php runs all three reads against a real database; verified failing with the exact production error before the change and passing after. The pre-existing unit test only covered log() and mocked DB::statement() to return true, so it could never have caught this.

NOT authored by this triage run. Verified tonight by running the covering suites (gdprAuditTranslations.test.ts + EnterpriseDashboard.test.tsx, 31 tests, all pass). 143723388.title: GDPR ALERT: data-subject requests pending past the response threshold
143723388.note: The alarm was correct and the backlog was real; it is now empty. Owner confirmed the 4 open requests were test data and authorised closing them. Read from production first: #6/#7/#8 (tenant 5) belonged to partner.demo+niamh@example.test, a reserved .test domain; #11 (tenant 11) belonged to a member account that had since been erased and anonymised, so nothing remained to rectify. NONE of the four was an erasure request, checked explicitly because marking an erasure 'completed' triggers a real irreversible Article 17 deletion. 143725191.title: Safeguarding contact gate unusable for tenants with live vetted-interaction selections

143797835.note: THE REAL MOBILE FAULT, needing a decision only the owner can take. expo-secure-store fails on every write: SecureStore.setItemAsync -> iOS Keychain -> "A required entitlement isn't present" (key nexus_tenant_slug, storage_op set). SOURCE IDENTIFIED, and it is almost certainly not a member: every event carries an iOS Simulator bundle path under /Users/runner/, X-Tenant-Slug partner-demo, a GitHub-Actions Azure IP and a US country code — which is exactly .github/workflows/ios-simulator-screenshots.yml (runs-on macos-15, EXPO_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_TENANT partner-demo, EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL https://api.project-nexus.ie). The unsigned Simulator build has no keychain-sharing entitlement, so the Keychain refuses it. Consequence in the app: mobile/lib/storage.ts set() caches in memory ONLY after a successful encrypted write, so a failed write persists nothing and the tenant slug is lost — the "random logouts" symptom that reporting was added to diagnose. Two decisions for the owner: (1) should the CI screenshot tour keep pointing at PRODUCTION, where its failures land in real error tracking; (2) does a non-secret value like the tenant slug belong in the Keychain at all, or should storage.set fall back to plain storage for non-secret keys so a missing entitlement cannot silently break persistence. Not fixed automatically: both are mobile build/ architecture choices, and an iOS build cannot be verified from this machine.

144002377.title: [APP LOG] Event: mobile_error | Version: 1.2.0 | Platform: mobile | Data: {"name":"Error","message":"Calling the 'setValueWithKeyAsync' function has failed\n\u2192 Caused by: A required entitlement isn't present.","stack":"Error: Calling the 'setValueWi...
144002377.note: FIXED (grouping only) in 9c36b61d1. This issue is one of THIRTY-ONE Sentry groups opened by a single mobile fault in four days — 31 of the 37 items in the 2026-09-01 triage queue. Root cause of the fan-out: POST /api/app/log built its Log::error message by embedding the client payload whole, including the JS `stack`, whose frames are absolute paths carrying a per-install CoreSimulator device and application UUID. Sentry groups a plain Log::error by message text, so identical faults never matched. Five sampled events were byte-identical except for those UUIDs. The message now carries the fault's identity only (event, version, platform plus bounded, key-sorted scalar fields); the full payload moves to log context and still reaches Sentry as the `log_context` extra. Three regression tests in AppControllerTest hold it, verified failing before the fix. NOT DEPLOYED. 🔴 The MOBILE fault itself is NOT fixed — see the needs-owner decision on NEXUS-PHP-67 (143797835).

144785932.title: Listing image upload failed
144785932.note: Real member harm, but the fix is bigger than a nightly change. A member (user 74, tenant 2) uploaded a 7173x9333 (66.9 megapixel) photo to listing 504. ImageUploader rejects anything over 25 MP as decompression-bomb protection, which is correct, but it throws a bare \Exception for validation refusals AND for genuine server faults alike. ListingsController::uploadImage catches everything and returns HTTP 500 with the generic 'Failed to upload image', so the member is never told the photo is too big and cannot fix it. Suggested fix: give ImageUploader a distinct validation exception, return 422 with a specific reason, and stop reporting member input refusals to Sentry as server errors. Needs a new translated string in all 11 locales plus a review of the other ~10 ImageUploader callers, so it is past the size a nightly run should attempt.
